sharedRules.casting: All fifteen retain Action and V/S/F. Use the actual casting class’s rank, school, minimum class level, independently acquired repertoire and base RP price. A legal cast commits costs, concentration transitions and ordinary Dissonance/Refrain before interruption. Failure, immunity, missing information and countering give no refund or restoration of old concentration. Use actual casting ability + PB for attacks and 8 + PB + that modifier for save DC; ordinary saves are binary. No generic upcast, additional Action or inferred class-card access.
sharedRules.time: Unless a card states otherwise, a minute ends at the caster’s tenth future original regular-start marker, excluding a start underway, or after 60 elapsed seconds if begun outside initiative. Retain original virtual markers or absolute deadlines through reorder, extra turns, absence and travel. Suppression never pauses a clock, refunds spent history or replays an application. Later saved-against casts do not dispel an older valid application. Extra turns do not supply extra periodic pulses, order opportunities or repeat saves.
sharedRules.information: Use actual established facts and each information protection’s real subject and generating-source scope. Hidden unprotected facts can be read; missing facts are not invented. An unavailable answer does not identify the hidden reason. Ordinary observed outcomes and inferences remain possible. No new faction roster, plane, moral axis, cosmic force, secret doctrine or guaranteed destiny is authored. Current accepted expedition/faction procedures now supply their actual records and social limits. This spell proposal grants no membership, standing, allied status, permission, roster or institution merely by requesting information.
sharedRules.control: A successfully established hard whole-Action/turn component spends the shared source-character/target/encounter guard once. Its continued valid duration does not claim a new allowance each turn. Initial prevention leaves no banked component; later suppression retains the existing clock and spent history. A blocked component gets no unprinted fallback. Actual component immunities remain separate; creature type alone is no blanket mental immunity. Limited attack or movement restrictions do not become whole-Action denial merely because alternatives are unattractive.
sharedRules.newControlBindings: NEW binding for Dominate Person and Confusion: use the reviewed Enchantment compelled-budget arbitration and shared six-second outside-initiative control cycle, preserving already spent budgets on entry to real initiative. A valid order/table instruction receives its priority timestamp when issued or generated at that opportunity; simultaneous instructions use application order then stable source ID. A losing instruction gets no second budget and does not erase an earlier mandate. Actual ordinary Attack Actions use native attacks unless the card expressly limits them to one. Only actual required ordinary ammunition can be compelled; no optional finite resource, spell/RP, recharge, charge, special expendable ammunition, permanent property surrender, protected secret, knowing binding-oath violation, direct self-harm or knowingly suicidal route can be forced. Bonus Actions, Reactions and extra Actions remain target-controlled. Hostile conduct uses ordinary initiative before execution, never a free virtual pre-initiative attack.
sharedRules.newCompanionBinding: NEW for an actually eligible Humanoid under Dominate Person, or any eligible Confusion target, using an owner-attached companion chassis: use the actual original-owner regular attached phase, original profile and structural command/offense caps. No independent turn, dominator companion allowance or unwilling owner Bonus Action is created. A pending command reservation can be redirected only for this same companion in this same phase, under the reviewed Dominate Beast bridge; spent or another companion’s reservation cannot be stolen. A repeat WIS save occurs at the end of that real regular attached phase even when no instruction executed; this source-specific checkpoint adds no ordinary START/END, recharge or other condition tick. If no such phase is currently supplied, only an END-only six-second save schedule continues, with no orders/actions. On transitioning to actual phases, map the next unresolved save to the next regular phase end, preserve resolved saves and the original maximum, and never replay an opportunity. This extension is proposed explicitly; it is not already conferred by Dominate Beast.
sharedRules.newEndSaveBinding: NEW: Overwhelming Grief, Charm Monster, Erase Emotion and Phantasmal Killer use affected regular-END saves, including an affected current turn, without extra-turn saves. Outside initiative their first END-only save is at application +6 seconds and then each six seconds. On entering initiative map the next unresolved save to the next actual regular END, retain completed saves and the original absolute maximum, and do not add an immediate transition save. For an owner-attached target, use its actual regular attached-phase end with the same END-only fallback/transition above, granting no actions. Dominate Person and Confusion instead use their shared behavior cycle and companion binding.
sharedRules.newCompanionPulseBinding: NEW for Illusion Phantasmal Killer on an owner-attached companion: its periodic packet uses the beginning of the actual original-owner regular attached phase, after that phase’s required processing, under the same once-per-numbered-round exposure. It creates no independent START or other start-trigger event. If no actual phase exists, use only the six-second damage schedule and original deadline, granting no actions. Transition to a real phase maps the next unresolved pulse opportunity without replaying an initial or completed pulse. Its separately scheduled repeat save still follows the END-only bridge.
sharedRules.DE4-GUARD-01: NEW scoped DE4-GUARD-01 amendment: Mark Omen, Fate Coin and Fate Reversal share one guard: an original roll event and its entire replacement lineage may receive at most one reroll from any of these three spells, across all casters, coins, marks, Fate Reversal permissions and recasts. Reserve this allowance at the first legal activation's commitment, not after the replacement die resolves. For a multi-die roll, the whole set/pool is one original roll event; the resulting attack's separate later damage roll is a different event. A shared area-damage roll remains one event even when applied to several creatures. Other exact class reroll features keep their own permissions and timing, but do not erase this guard or create a fresh lineage for these three spells. If competing declarations are simultaneous, use current initiative order; outside initiative use stable actor IDs then stable source/application IDs fixed before the original event, with the same stable tie-break for initiative ties. Only the first legal commitment spends its own actual mark, coin or Fate Reversal permission and any Reaction required by that source; a later declaration barred by this guard spends nothing. No new Action, roll event, cast, payment or duplicated outcome hook is created by replacing dice. This guard extension and the explicitly proposed DE4-RNG-05 digital mapping preserve each source's distinct replacement unit and eligibility. Mark Omen still replaces the caster's own marked-target attack d20 procedure with no additional Action or Reaction; Fate Coin still changes exactly one eligible engine RNG die component through its holder's actual Reaction and30-foot perceived-event interface; Fate Reversal still requires its own Reaction, pending permission, eligible complete attack/save/check d20 procedure and60-foot perceived-event interface. No class feature is added to this family merely because it changes a roll, and this amendment grants no new access to hidden dice or any source's otherwise ineligible roll. Apply DE4-RNG-05 in full; its player-information boundaries never grant hidden RNG access.
sharedRules.DE4-SEAL-LOCI-02: NEW spell-specific proposal for Seal Vision only. In creature mode use the protected actual body; in area mode a body is protected when any actual portion is within the20ft sphere and has center LoE, and a discrete spatial magical expression is protected at its actual source-defined locus. No whole-plane, body-independent soul or remote caster concentration locus is inferred. For an ongoing body-target Divination buff/mark, suspend that target component while protected, preserve identity/deadline/history, and resume only a still-existing component when protection ends. For a pending personal Divination permission, an actually protected/suppressed holder cannot activate that permission. For a Divination-created Fate Coin inside the area, retain the actual same physical coin/HP/custody/deadline while disabling its magical reroll use; do not create material or destroy it merely from this spell suppression. Prevent an actually blocked new Divination component from establishing; no deferred component appears when protection later ends. For a reroll use whose own source remains operative, separately test the actual original roll-generating creature/object or source-defined local event. Protecting one recipient of an independently generated shared damage pool does not split or selectively reroll that pool, and ordinary indirect consequences retain their original source school. The original roll generator/event is fixed by the actual source before a reroll; it is not the rendered RNG animation position or a convenient alternative victim. If a source leaves that generator genuinely undefined, resolve and record that ambiguity before claiming a legal protected/unprotected example. Known non-operative permission is unusable without expenditure. An otherwise legal operative permission committed against a protected original roll event is spent under its real source and common guard, but its blocked Divination alteration produces no replacement; the unchanged original result resolves. This latter paid-block distinction is explicit NEW local authorship requiring joint review. No information-only ward becomes general antimagic.
sharedRules.DE4-ORDER-DELIVERY-02: NEW scoped Dominate Person mental-order channel: a conscious controller can issue the one opportunity order only while controller and target are on the same actual plane. No additional maintained range or shared language/hearing is required; no perceptions/location/knowledge flow back. Protection against an actual information-gathering source does not by itself cancel this noninformational channel. A genuinely issued valid order retains its ordinary opportunity and exact expiry if the target is subsequently relocated; a later failed new issuance creates no replacement. This does not transport the target, permit an unsafe route or compel optional resource use. Dominate Person uses the future START/actual attached-phase opportunity, so it does not grant an advance stored order outside those specific source timings. Compulsion stores a fixed world-space direction on its actual application plane. If the target is on another plane at its sole execution opportunity, the direction instruction has no executable route and expires without refund or delayed retry; no universal cross-plane compass relation is invented. Same-plane relocation keeps the recorded world direction, not a new vector to the caster.
sharedRules.DE4-NIGHTMARE-ROOT-02: NEW source-specific implementation of the accepted Null root rule. On a failed Phantasmal Killer application with a legally established damage component, create that recipient/application damage root before its first packet and snapshot the actual caster dealer's current unsuppressed Null Veil. The Illusion immediate packet and all later scheduled packets of that application descend from this one root, even if its initial round exposure was already spent and no initial packet resolved. Later Veil changes never rewrite this root. A genuinely new spell application, including a separate Enchantment immediate hit, creates a new root and checks the then-current caster state. Allocating a root is not damage, a hit, a Wound, a kill, a resource event or a claimed periodic exposure. Use actual scheduled recipient lifecycles, death saves and preexisting-source timing; a companion phase is not a new regular turn.
sharedRules.DE4-COMPULSION-EXPIRY-03: NEW DE4-COMPULSION-EXPIRY-03, scoped only to Compulsion: at successful failed-save establishment record one pending instruction, its application order, original timing basis and one finite latest opportunity marker. For a creature with a regular turn schedule, use its next future regular START, excluding a turn already underway. For an owner-attached chassis, use the attached-phase boundary after the next original-owner regular turn that has not begun; record the original regular owner END/attached-phase marker even if an actual phase may be unavailable then. If no such original schedule/marker exists, use application+6 elapsed seconds. These are spell-only timing records, not new creature turns. Preserve the original marker and its virtual elapsed-time mapping through initiative changes, absence, extra turns and relocation. Use at most one qualifying future actual movement opportunity within that window; an attached target can execute only in its real source-authorized original-owner regular attached phase. An already-underway owner turn supplies no newly compelled phase. A genuinely earlier qualifying opportunity after a schedule change can consume the instruction once, with only its actual remaining budget. A later rescheduling cannot carry the instruction past its original finite marker. At the recorded boundary, finish ordinary required START/phase processing before this instruction's sole eligibility/movement check; immediately after that check expire it whether movement was possible, blocked, suppressed or zero. This specifically typed expiry-after-opportunity ordering avoids expiring the instruction before its own simultaneous check; it is not a change to global phase0 duration expiry. When the actual lifecycle supplies no qualifying phase at the recorded boundary, perform an expiry-only bookkeeping check at that original marker and remove the instruction. This check grants no movement, Action, Reaction, recharge, control START, command or owner resource expenditure. An owner-attached target with no original schedule therefore expires at application+6 if no independently supplied lawful phase occurs first. A normal independent creature outside initiative can have the one expressly proposed ordinary movement opportunity by application+6 under the real shared behavior budget; establish initiative before hostile behavior. No phase, target physiology, missing movement mode or new budget is inferred from that fallback. A later repair, owner return, phase creation or suppression ending never replays an expired instruction. This is explicit NEW joint-review authorship, not an already accepted general timing rule.
sharedRules.DE4-RNG-05:
NEW DE4-RNG-05 proposal under the owner's video-game-only directive. Authored dice are engine RNG operations, not physical tabletop objects. The actual conjured Fate Coin remains its existing physical game-world item with the same body, custody, hand, HP, duration and consumption. A roll event has an immutable original-event ID, replacement-lineage ID, actual generating entity/local event, original source, stable ordered component IDs, original modifiers/advantage state, target set and source-defined visibility grants. Finish the complete original RNG operation before any of these reroll permissions can commit; commit before its consequences. Fate Coin selects exactly one component of the complete eligible original operation and draws the same die type once; recompute its original reduction/selection with every other component unchanged. Mark Omen and Fate Reversal replace their own complete eligible d20 procedure. These distinctions survive digital implementation.

An engine's knowledge, logging, debug access, animation, a player's camera, knowledge of the seed, or prediction of a hidden outcome grants no character/player permission. The entire original die-result set must already be available to the acting player under the original event's established gameplay-information policy, and the source's actual perception, range, line-of-effect and resource predicates must independently pass. No eligible prompt, selectable event identifier or failure reason may reveal an otherwise hidden event. If the original source has no established visibility grant, these spells grant none; a source-specific presentation decision must be authored separately. A visible summed total alone does not reveal otherwise hidden component faces or grant a one-component choice. A fixed or automatic result with no actual RNG operation supplies no reroll event. Source-defined finite uniform 1dN random draws are eligible for Fate Coin only when their original result set is already available and the other source predicates pass; an empty set creates no draw, and the previously snapshotted candidate set never changes on replacement. Arbitrary simulation RNG, generation seeds and unexposed loot/world generation are not made eligible merely by existing in engine memory. No additional replacement RNG is consumed for a rejected preflight or a paid-but-blocked alteration; record the committed cost and guard separately from whether a new draw occurred.

Serialize legal commitments through the actual gameplay event queue. Simultaneous candidates use current initiative order; ties use stable preexisting actor ID then stable source/application ID. Outside initiative use those stable actor/source IDs fixed before this original event was generated. Network arrival, frame rate, client/UI order, reopening a prompt and a new replacement ID cannot change priority or create a new original lineage. A rejected later candidate spends no Reaction, token or permission. This is a scoped deterministic tie-break for these three spell permissions, not a rewrite of all interrupt priority or any class-specific reroll. Snapshot the original modifiers, including any eligible Alignment Nexus benefit, when the original roll is created; replacement retains those modifiers even if later alignment/ward changes would alter a genuinely new event. Apply only the final original event's consequences once. No additional cast, attack, target rescan, payment, hit, Wound, death event or resource grant is generated by a replacement.

SOURCE POLICY BINDING: DE4-PRESENTATION-06 in this same pending revision supplies only its five explicitly proposed entries. Unlisted events remain denied. Both documents require exact joint acceptance before live application.
sharedRules.DE4-PRESENTATION-06:
NEW DE4-PRESENTATION-06 — proposed narrow digital presentation policy for this conference; NOT an already accepted visibility grant. This policy grants only the following event-result presentations. It does not disclose hidden creatures, secret events, source/rank/DC/AC information, hidden modifier reasons, RNG seeds or future draws. An explicit source prohibition on disclosure takes precedence. Unlisted or unclassified events remain unavailable to these three Fate permissions until separately authored; absence of a secrecy tag is not a grant.

1. OVERT-ATTACK: for an actual ordinary Core attack whose generating creature, declared attack and target are already perceived/identified by the reacting creature through its real senses, give that creature's authorized controller the complete resolved original attack d20 set before hit/miss consequences. This is an explicit new result-presentation decision, not a new sensing ability. Display the faces and which original selection rule is being applied, not the hidden causes of advantage, the target's AC or hidden modifiers. A hidden attacker or an unperceived/unknown target does not qualify under this entry. An extra camera, spectator role, battle log or engine access is not perception. An AI controller receives only the corresponding authorized view, not the entire engine state.

2. OWN-REQUESTED-CHECK: an actually requested, nonsecret ordinary ability/skill/tool check presents its complete original d20 set privately to that actor's authorized controller. Automatic/secret sensing checks, protected inquiries and hidden contests are excluded. Another reacting character can use that player's legitimate display only when that reacting character independently satisfies its own actual source perception/range/LoE and resource predicates; this rule grants no character-to-character telepathy. In a multi-character player party, the player may control both actors; a multiplayer peer does not inherit another player's private grant.

3. BURNING-HANDS-DAMAGE: once an actual reviewed Burning Hands cone is manifested and the shared 3d6 operation is generated, present the complete shared faces before damage consequences to the caster's controller and to controllers of reacting characters who actually perceive the caster and the manifested cone. This whitelist entry is specifically for the reviewed Burning Hands damage operation, not every damage pool. It reveals no target list, save result, resistance or hidden recipient. Per-recipient damage is still computed once from the one final shared total. A reaction holder must additionally pass its own actual Coin range/LoE/hand/custody predicates. A source-suppressed operation that creates no actual damage draw gives nothing to reroll.

4. CONFUSION-BEHAVIOR: for this pending Confusion procedure, show the actual finite d4 behavior, any genuinely generated d8 direction, and any genuinely generated uniform 1dN perceived-target selection privately to the affected body's authorized controller before that behavior executes. Do not expose candidates that this body cannot actually perceive. Other controllers receive no raw selection results under this entry. A player who also controls a reacting holder can use that legitimate result view only if the reacting holder independently perceives the true roll-generating body and passes Coin's other source requirements. The snapshotted set and candidate order are immutable; an empty set makes no draw. A private NPC-controller view is not disclosed to human players.

5. RESONANCE-WELL-RESERVE: show the actual initial 1d4 reserve-creation draw privately to the Well creator's authorized controller before the reserve is established. This preserves the existing timing boundary but authors its digital display; it does not expose any already-established or hidden reserve and does not permit a later reroll/refill. The reacting holder still needs Coin's real event perception/range/LoE/custody/Reaction.

For these entries only, record policyId, entryId, original event ID, the authorized controller set and the actual perception evidence at generation. Recheck the reacting source's own spatial/resource predicates at commitment. Already lawfully learned original faces are not erased by a later effect, but event knowledge alone never satisfies a currently missing character predicate. Present only information this whitelist actually grants, whether or not any observer possesses a Fate source; resource possession cannot become a detector. Total-only or hidden-result policies remain insufficient. Preserve the original RNG component IDs and reduction rule through replacement. No rejected declaration or paid-but-blocked alteration generates a replacement draw.

This is a minimum concrete policy, not a universal dice-visibility policy. In particular, unlisted enemy saving throws, trauma, secret checks, loot/world generation and private source operations remain unavailable. Future presentation entries require explicit source-specific authorship and separate review. Composition vectors that declare a visibility grant remain composition vectors; that declaration is not evidence that an unlisted live source supplies one.

NEW BURNING-HANDS EVENT-EXISTENCE COMPLETION FOR CONCURRENCE: For this source only, each actually manifested Burning Hands cone generates exactly one complete original shared3d6 operation at its ordinary damage-resolution checkpoint whether the eligible recipient set is empty, entirely hidden, or includes known recipients. It is the same cast operation, not an extra roll, attack or damage packet per recipient. A cast interrupted or prevented before manifestation generates none. A manifested empty cone deals no damage and triggers no hit/damage/Wound/kill/resource consequence, even though its finite original pool is available under BURNING-HANDS-DAMAGE. Thus the presence, number, values, availability and timing of the published pool do not encode whether hidden recipients exist. No target list, saves, defenses or damage outcome is added to this presentation. A paid Coin may alter that original empty-cone pool only through its ordinary actual predicates, with its normal consumed item/Reaction/guard and no refunded cost; it creates no recipient or successful damage event. This is explicit NEW per-source RNG-generation authorship, not a rule for other empty areas or unlisted spells.
